sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201], a cyclical path rather than a straight line.
The first step change came in FY2017 and FY2018, when revenue rose 18.0% and then 20.4% [D42][D92], lifting operating margin from 3.0% to 15.2% [F21][F23].
The FY2017 increase was primarily due to higher sales volume from improved end-user demand, plus favorable dealer inventory changes [P68].
FY2020 reversed hard, with revenue down 22.4% [D198] on lower end-user demand and dealer destocking across all three primary segments [P59].
The recovery peaked in FY2023, when operating margin reached 19.3% [F28] on 12.8% revenue growth [D357], before FY2025 gave back 3.7pp of margin [D476].
In FY2025 Power & Energy was the engine, contributing 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue growth [D759][D463] on 11.6% segment growth and a 47.6% share of revenue [D758][D757].
Power Generation alone grew 32.5% and added 3.9pp [D894][D895], while Construction Industries subtracted 0.6pp [D766] and Resource Industries was flat [D779].
The consolidated increase was primarily driven by higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025 [D489], at 9.1% [D481], so incremental operating margin was -69.1% [D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% against a 17.7% net income decline [D467][D465], as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 [F30] sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1123][D1122].

The 3.7pp decline [D476] came mostly from cost of revenue, a -4.2pp effect [D490], as operating profit fell on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P9].
Those manufacturing costs largely reflected the impact of higher tariffs [P9], while SG&A and R&D effects were roughly neutral at -0.0pp and +0.1pp [D492][D491].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% [F50] sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin [F30], with a 24.0% effective tax rate [D449] and $892 million of other income [X110].

Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D450], while free cash flow of $8.9 billion was 1.00x net income [F100][F40][D451], above the 0.96x free-cash-flow-to-net-income window median [D1135].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion [F100][D469], a 13.2% margin [D447] below the 13.4% peer median [D1148].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion [F90][D470], 1.25x D&A [D452], and the investing outflow widened on higher capital expenditures [P3].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow still rose, primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
The company carried net debt of $26.2 billion at FY2025 [D456], net cash of -38.8% of revenue [D457] against a -35.6% peer median [D1152].
That is the third straight year of deeper net debt, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D350], as total debt grew 14.1% [D485] and cash rose 44.9% [D484].
Liquidity is adequate, with a 1.44x current ratio [F180] above the 1.40x window median [D1138], and return on average equity of 43.5% [D462] far above the 23.3% peer median [D1156].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion [X140][X150] were 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted count fell 3.5% [D483].
Net cash fell for a second year into net debt in FY2025, reaching -$26.2 billion from -$22.1 billion in FY2023 [R1][D350][D456].
The leverage is modest against equity of $21.3 billion [F200], but the direction removes a cushion if tariffs keep pressuring margins.
Revenue declined 3.4% in FY2024 [R2][D410] on lower sales volume, partly offset by favorable price realization [P22].
One down year in a cyclical machinery business is not alarming by itself, and FY2025 growth of 4.3% [D463] reversed it.
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy statement rather than the 10-K, differing by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins and cash conversion, but the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters.
Whether operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the 14.3% window median [D1123] or falls toward the 16.5% FY2025 level [F30] as tariff costs persist.
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 13.2% FY2025 level [D447] or stays below the 13.4% peer median [D1148] as capex runs at 4.2% of revenue [D446].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue in the FY2026 10-K improves from -38.8% [D457] or deepens past the -41.5% FY2022 level [D298].
